title: Operating evidence gate for a 3–5 year Intel short, November 5, 2026
scope: Review whether new primary evidence warrants replacing the frozen strong recovery policy with the prior weak-demand diagnostic. No forecasts, original model files, or PDF changed. No probability fitted to the quote or short-return threshold.

verdict.decision: Do not promote the weak-demand diagnostic to the central forecast on the currently reviewed evidence.
verdict.why: A weaker trajectory is economically plausible, but latest industry and issuer evidence points to rapid server demand, constrained supply and continuing premium-product adoption. Competitive entry and historical pricing reversals justify a material downside scenario. They do not identify that scenario as more likely than the stronger path.
verdict.strongest_current_anchor: 2027 Intel unit growth of 20% is consistent with the TrendForce global industry/share forecast. The exact 20% ASP growth assumption is substantially less identified and remains a judgment.
verdict.not_proven: Neither the strong policy nor the weak policy has an empirically estimated scenario probability. Current evidence does not establish absolute short profit over 3–5 years. A weak case that creates profit cannot validate its own selection.
verdict.competition_use: Defend the evidence gap explicitly: the pitch currently demonstrates demanding valuation/return assumptions and sensitivity, rather than a source-established central path to a lower 2030 share price.

sources.locator: PDF page 6 (zero-index 5), outlook; page 7 (zero-index 6), segment guidance and capex
sources.novelty: Rechecked existing primary evidence; newly emphasized difference from TrendForce forecast.
sources.facts: Management expects industry server CPU units to grow more than 30% in both 2026 and 2027, with industry supply constraints through 2027 into 2028. Q4 DCAI revenue is guided to mid-teens sequential growth. PC TAM is expected to decline roughly 10% in 2027. Gross capex is expected to rise strongly in 2027 from about $20B in 2026.
sources.implication: Industry guidance is not Intel-specific shipment guidance. Weak PC demand is already substantially allowed for in the frozen client forecast and is not evidence of weak server demand. Do not turn the greater-than-30% lower boundary into a measured point estimate.

sources.locator: MD&A printed pages 31 and 33–34; Future Node Development and Manufacturing Expansion Projects
sources.novelty: Revalidated prior pricing and supply evidence.
sources.facts: Q3 server ASP rose 54% and units 10% year over year. Premium mix drove most ASP growth; pricing contributed less and partly offset input costs. Data-center demand exceeds available supply for some products; substrates and other constraints may persist into 2027. Intel committed to completing 14A for future internal products, while expansion scale also depends on external design wins.
sources.implication: Supports a premium-mix/recovery path but not exact 2027 ASP growth or a consolidated incremental margin. Shared 14A development is not exclusively a cost of hypothetical merchant business.

sources.locator: Opening shipment forecast, Intel supply paragraph, accompanying supplier-share chart; chart visually verified in prior judge review
sources.facts: Projects global server CPU shipments up 31% in 2026 and more than 40% in 2027. Chart puts Intel share at 50% then 42%; Arm-based global share approaches 30% in 2027. Intel process, packaging and manufacturing constraints are already reasons given for declining share.
sources.implication: The same forecast that highlights competition supports approximately 18% or greater Intel unit growth at the 40% industry boundary. Do not count its share-loss argument a second time as a new cut from the 20% model.

sources.locator: Shareholder letter printed page 2 (zero-index PDF page 1), final paragraphs; printed page 3 opening paragraph
sources.novelty: New primary issuer evidence after the prior full-hour review.
sources.facts: Arm reports multiple-customer AGI CPU purchase orders extending through calendar 2027, first commercial deliveries on track for fiscal Q4 2027, and increased confidence in up to $2B of silicon revenue across fiscal 2027–28. Oracle plans AGI CPU instances in 2027. The letter separately forecasts Arm-based share above 60% at top hyperscalers by calendar year-end 2026.
sources.limitations: No cancellation rights, deposits, minimum obligations, unit quantities, pricing, or annual split of the up-to-$2B figure are disclosed. The revenue outlook is not stated to be entirely covered by noncancellable orders. Fiscal Q4 2027 corresponds to January–March 2027. Top-hyperscaler share is not the global CPU denominator, and its precise market-share measurement is not defined here.
sources.implication: Raises confidence in actual competitive entry versus announcements alone. Does not quantify displacement of Intel, distinguish substitution from newly created demand, or establish a weaker central Intel forecast.

sources.locator: Opening CPU/DDR5 discussion and paragraphs on ODM shortages and Murata expansion
sources.novelty: Additional primary market-research cross-check, not a separate Intel sales forecast.
sources.facts: Reports AI inference and agents increasing CPU and associated DDR5/power-component demand. ODMs expect high-end MLCC shortages to be most severe in Q1–Q2 2027; additional Murata capacity is unlikely before 2028.
sources.implication: System bottlenecks can limit shipments or increase costs, while also corroborating robust demand. No quantified Intel unit/ASP impact is disclosed; no extra cut should be mechanically layered onto a forecast already constrained by components.

sources.locator: MD&A Intel Products, 2025 versus 2024; Sales Arrangements printed page 13
sources.novelty: Already included in frozen policy; re-used as a genuine counterargument.
sources.facts: Recast 2024 server ASP rose 11% while units fell 8%; 2025 ASP declined 4% while units increased 9%, with competitive pricing/lower-core mix. General product purchase orders can be cancelled, changed or delayed with little notice and without penalty.
sources.implication: Blended ASP and unit growth need not move together. Scarcity and announced capacity do not make premium pricing permanent. Historical reversals demonstrate a mechanism, not its 2027 probability; general PO terms do not override undisclosed specific LTAs.

sources.novelty: Already investigated during prior hour; not counted as new.
sources.facts: Named customer plans custom SoCs on Intel 18A-P, initially a high-performance compute chiplet. No program revenue, production volume, launch date or exclusivity is disclosed.
sources.implication: The commercial option is real. A claim of no external customers is untenable; a large cash-flow award is not yet quantified.

unit_growth_boundary_diagnostic.formula: Intel unit growth = (1 + global unit growth) * (2027 Intel share / 2026 Intel share) - 1
unit_growth_boundary_diagnostic.interpretation: 10% Intel unit growth can be reconciled with approximately 31% industry growth and 42% share. This combines the low end of Intel industry guidance with another forecaster's share path; it is a plausible cautious scenario, not a joint published forecast or probability estimate. At 40–45% industry growth and unchanged 42% share, implied Intel growth is 17.6–21.8%. No 2028–30 issuer unit-growth path was found.

ASP_identification.observed: Frozen primary-source bridge is Q1/Q2/Q3 2026 ASP +27/+48/+54% year over year; latest YTD +44%. These compare different prior-year quarters and customer/product mixes.
ASP_identification.identity: Annual ASP equals annual CPU revenue divided by annual CPU units. Exit carryover equals an exit ASP divided by the prior annual unit-weighted ASP, minus one.
ASP_identification.missing: Public rounded YoY shipment and ASP changes do not identify absolute quarterly shipments, exact 2026 unit weights, same-SKU pricing, customer discounts, or Q4 2026 exit ASP. Q4 actual results are not yet available at this cutoff.
ASP_identification.what_can_be_defended: Positive carryover and richer 2027 product mix are plausible. A slowdown from the 2026 YoY increases is sensible as comparisons toughen and premium penetration rises. Both 10% and 20% 2027 blended ASP growth can be defended as scenarios; the reviewed information does not prove one is the measured carryover.
ASP_identification.what_cannot_be_defended: Claiming 20% is mathematically locked in, averaging quarterly YoY growth rates to estimate carryover, treating every price increase as pure profit, or using the 19.1667% revenue-restoration threshold as evidence for the forecast.
ASP_identification.chronology: The prior policy disclosed that the 19.1667% offset diagnostic was known before the 20% ASP judgment. New review does not erase that history. Keep independent operating rationale and sensitivity visible.

path_comparison.interpretation: The weak scenario still grows server revenue at 16.17% annually through 2030, but ends 33.18% below the strong path. It is a persistent multiyear level shortfall, not just a temporary shipment delay; prior weak policy carries that lower level beyond 2030. Continued future growth does not make the relative miss small.

margin_evidence_gate.known: The frozen policy applies 50% consolidated incremental EBIT retention to extra server revenue through 2030; the weak diagnostic applies 50% decremental retention. These are modeled marginal economics, not issuer guidance.
margin_evidence_gate.support_for_recovery: Recent premium mix and manufacturing learning support operating leverage; the old policy documented roughly 69% product-profit retention on the Q3 revenue bridge, with 50% reserved for forward costs.
margin_evidence_gate.limits: Reported product profit excludes some consolidated costs and varies with transfer pricing. Higher-core products cost more, price increases partly compensate input inflation, new-node costs can offset ASP, and fixed costs make a demand miss expensive. None identifies a precise future consolidated decremental margin. Existing Foundry dollar profits must not receive duplicate absorption credits or losses.
margin_evidence_gate.capital_asymmetry: Some capital, substrate and minimum-production commitments persist if orders weaken. Preserve lagged capex flexibility and actual working-capital mechanics; do not assume every revenue miss frees cash proportionately. Those commitments are generally within existing budgets, not automatically additional expenditures.

external_merchant_wafer_upside.status: Retain an explicit option/risk discussion. No source in this review supports deleting the option or assigning a numerical success probability.
external_merchant_wafer_upside.prior_funded_diagnostic: Prior policy with $10B merchant revenue in 2033, 10% annual growth through 2040, 40% EBIT margin and 1.0 incremental capital turnover added $4.20065 per share under the corrected maturing-risk curve, moving central end-2026 value from $53.77048 to $57.97113. This was a favorable funded sensitivity, not a new base forecast or horizon price.
external_merchant_wafer_upside.risk_controls: Do not double count existing packaging profit, shared 14A R&D, or capacity already serving Intel products. Shared infrastructure can improve returns, but third-party production can displace internal output. Fund incremental investment and working capital. No binding contract is required for every forecast; unreported economics remain judgments.

evidence_that_would_change_selection: A consistent revision in industry shipment forecasts and Intel capacity/output that makes the lower unit path central, with the global share denominator reconciled.
Accepted shipment mix, realized ASP and customer pricing evidence showing premium growth slowing materially relative to the frozen path, distinguishing mix from discounts and cost pass-through.
Customer migration measured in deployed CPU units or spending that exceeds the share loss already assumed, rather than counting announcements or all Arm-based spending as displaced Intel revenue.
A persistent margin/cash miss after isolating one-time disruptions and without double-counting Foundry absorption or working-capital advances.
Conversely, successful Clearwater/Diamond adoption, continued premium pricing and funded external wafer awards would weaken an absolute short even if the current required-return critique remains.
search_limits: Latest available Intel financial results checked were Q3 2026; no newer Intel operating guidance was identified as of the Nov5 review. Arm Nov4 letter was obtained directly. AMD Nov3 release was rechecked but already covered by prior research; no new exact AMD 2027 claim was adopted from secondary transcripts. Qualcomm Nov4 primary release text was not located in the indexed/accessible results, so unverified earnings claims were excluded.
mutations: Only this new operating_evidence.json was written by this child for the follow-up.
